bull.t: Rapid revenue scaling with high gross margins
bull.b: CoreWeave's top-line growth has been extraordinary, moving from under $0.3B to over $5B in two years while maintaining ~70%+ gross margins. Durable demand for GPU compute and stable unit economics support sustained revenue expansion and gross-profitability over the next several quarters, underpinning reinvestment and scale advantages.

bull.t: Large contracted backlog and signed commitments
bull.b: A near-$100B backlog with a high fraction contracted multi-year provides rare revenue visibility in cloud infrastructure. Significant multi-year commitments and >3.5GW contracted capacity reduce churn and demand uncertainty, enabling predictable revenue recognition, capacity planning and a clearer path to ARR targets over the medium term.

bull.t: Strong operating cash generation and high adjusted margins
bull.b: Operating cash flow has increased materially alongside revenue, and management reports sizable adjusted EBITDA and margins. Robust core cash generation relative to underlying operations signals healthy unit economics and helps finance ongoing capacity buildouts, improving the company's ability to service obligations if maintained.

bear.t: Heavy leverage and rising debt levels
bear.b: Debt has increased sharply, leaving the balance sheet highly leveraged. Elevated leverage magnifies refinancing, covenant and interest-rate risk, constraining financial flexibility to absorb shocks or fund further buildouts without additional external financing, and raising the stakes on execution and margin recovery.

bear.t: Very negative free cash flow due to massive CapEx needs
bear.b: Persistent large negative free cash flow driven by multibillion-dollar capex programs forces ongoing external funding. Sustained negative FCF increases dilution and interest burdens, elevates execution risk on timely buildouts, and makes long-term returns highly dependent on capacity ramp efficiency and stable component costs.

bear.t: Large GAAP losses and rising interest expense
bear.b: Wide GAAP losses and sharply higher interest expense compress reported profitability and limit retained earnings. Rising interest costs increase leverage sensitivity to rates and delay sustainable GAAP profitability, meaning operating improvements must outpace financing costs to produce durable shareholder returns.
